articles.title: SJAA Sponsors First California Star Party
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) successfully sponsored the inaugural California Star Party (CSP) at Lake San Antonio on September 29-30, attracting around 80 telescopes and participants from across California. The event was deemed a great success, fostering a friendly atmosphere with attendees hoping it becomes an annual tradition. The article also includes detailed observing reports from the CSP and lists upcoming SJAA activities for November and December.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This article explores the similarities between terrestrial volcanic domes, specifically Lassen Peak, and lunar domes, such as the Marius Hills and Rumker complex. It explains their common formation processes involving magma pressure and vents, and how visiting Earth-based domes can provide a valuable perspective and 'feel' for understanding the geology and appearance of lunar features, despite some environmental differences. The author encourages observing Lassen Peak as a unique local laboratory for 'lunaphiles'.

articles.title: Leonids Made Easy
articles.summary: This article provides practical guidance for observing the annual Leonid meteor shower, which peaks around November 17-18 as Earth crosses Comet Temple-Tuttle's orbit. It encourages readers to watch from home, despite the full moon, emphasizing the potential for a significant meteor storm. Tips include identifying the radiant in Leo and distinguishing Leonids from other meteors.

articles.title: Planetary Observations
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for November 2000, focusing on the oppositions of Jupiter and Saturn. It offers detailed tips for observing Saturn's rings and Jupiter's atmospheric features, including satellite transits and shadow eclipses, alongside specific dates for these events. The author also briefly mentions the visibility of other planets such as Mercury, Venus, Uranus, Neptune, and Mars, encouraging readers to use telescopes to explore the 'bountiful planetary cornucopia'.

articles.title: December Holiday Party
articles.summary: The club's December general meeting will be a holiday party and social occasion on December 9th at 8 PM. Attendees are encouraged to bring potluck contributions, show-and-tell items (astro equipment, photos, software), and an anonymously wrapped astronomical gift for a "white elephant" exchange. The event promises fun activities and conversation.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar November 2000
articles.summary: This Celestial Calendar for November 2000 provides detailed astronomical data, including lunar phases, planetary positions, magnitudes, and rise/transit/set times for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. It also lists hours of darkness, astronomical twilight times, and sidereal time, highlighting November 25th as the darkest Saturday night. The document concludes with descriptions and photos of astronomy club members' projects, such as a meteor photo, a unique dobsonian telescope, a heliostat, and a star party information box.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Scope Status document provides an update on the availability of telescopes for members of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It lists scopes available for immediate loan, those currently out on regular or extended loan with due dates, and contact information for borrowing. The document also includes a waiting list for popular scopes.
